status: Proposition titles are quoted from the Secretary of State's Official Voter Information Guide. Your sample ballot is the final word.
statewideNote: Every California voter decides these 14 Propositions.

statewide.title: $11.25 billion in borrowing for affordable housing and veterans' home loans
statewide.what: AUTHORIZES BONDS FOR HOUSING AFFORDABILITY PROGRAMS. LEGISLATIVE STATUTE.
statewide.yes: The state can borrow $11.25 billion for affordable housing and veterans' home loans, repaid at about $500 million to $600 million a year.
statewide.no: The state does not borrow this $11.25 billion for housing and veterans' home loans.
statewide.needs: a simple majority of the votes cast on it

statewide.title: Lets the state save more in its emergency reserve
statewide.what: INCREASES STATE’S RAINY DAY FUND. LEGISLATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
statewide.yes: The state's rainy day fund can grow to 20% of its main tax money instead of 10%, and extra debt payments continue to 2040.
statewide.no: The rainy day fund stays capped at 10%, and the extra debt payments end in 2030.
statewide.needs: a simple majority of the votes cast on it

statewide.title: Makes the extra income tax on the highest earners permanent
statewide.what: PROVIDES PERMANENT FUNDING FOR SCHOOLS AND HEALTH CARE BY EXTENDING EXISTING TAX ON HIGH INCOMES. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
statewide.yes: The extra income tax on income above about $371,000 (single) or $742,000 (joint) becomes permanent instead of ending.
statewide.no: The extra income tax on high incomes expires as scheduled in 2031.
statewide.needs: a simple majority of the votes cast on it

statewide.title: Lets state and local governments give public money to candidates' campaigns
statewide.what: REPEALS PROHIBITION AGAINST PUBLIC FUNDING OF ELECTION CAMPAIGNS. LEGISLATIVE STATUTE.
statewide.yes: The state, counties and cities may create programs that give public money to qualifying candidates, within set limits.
statewide.no: The ban stays: the state and most local governments still cannot give public money to campaigns.
statewide.needs: a simple majority of the votes cast on it

statewide.title: Removes the replacement-candidate question from recall elections
statewide.what: CHANGES RECALL ELECTION PROCESS FOR STATEWIDE OFFICERS. LEGISLATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
statewide.yes: A recall ballot would only ask whether to remove the official; the seat would be filled by the normal vacancy rules.
statewide.no: Recall ballots keep asking both whether to remove the official and who should replace them.
statewide.needs: a simple majority of the votes cast on it

statewide.title: State-backed loans to help middle-income buyers of new homes
statewide.what: CREATES LOAN PROGRAM FOR MIDDLE-INCOME BUYERS OF QUALIFIED NEW HOMES. INITIATIVE STATUTE.
statewide.yes: The state housing agency can borrow up to $25 billion to lend buyers of new homes up to 17% of the price, repaid by the buyers.
statewide.no: No new state loan program for buyers of new homes is created.
statewide.needs: a simple majority of the votes cast on it

statewide.title: $8.4 billion in borrowing for immune-system medical research
statewide.what: AUTHORIZES BONDS FOR IMMUNOLOGY MEDICAL RESEARCH. INITIATIVE STATUTE.
statewide.yes: The state can borrow $8.4 billion for immunology research, repaid at about $500 million to $600 million a year for 20 years.
statewide.no: The state does not borrow $8.4 billion for immunology research.
statewide.needs: a simple majority of the votes cast on it

statewide.title: ID to vote in person, ID numbers on mail ballots, and citizenship checks
statewide.what: PROHIBITS CITIZENS FROM VOTING UNLESS THEY PRESENT GOVERNMENT-ISSUED IDENTIFICATION. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
statewide.yes: You would show government ID to vote in person and write the last 4 digits of an ID number on your mail ballot envelope.
statewide.no: Voters keep proving who they are by signature, with no ID number needed on mail ballots.
statewide.needs: a simple majority of the votes cast on it

statewide.title: One-time 5% tax on the wealth of California billionaires, mainly for health care
statewide.what: IMPOSES ONE-TIME TAX ON CERTAIN TAXPAYERS. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT AND STATUTE.
statewide.yes: California billionaires pay a one-time tax of up to 5% of their covered assets, mostly for health care.
statewide.no: No wealth tax on billionaires is charged.
statewide.needs: a simple majority of the votes cast on it

statewide.title: State Auditor reviews of new special taxes; new taxes count under the spending limit
statewide.what: PROHIBITS NEW STATE TAXES THAT EXCLUDE REVENUES FROM STATE SPENDING LIMIT. REQUIRES AUDITS FOR NEW STATE SPECIAL TAXES. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
statewide.yes: New special taxes get State Auditor reviews before the vote and every 4 years after, and new taxes count under the spending limit.
statewide.no: No new audit rules, and the spending-limit rules for new taxes stay as they are.
statewide.needs: a simple majority of the votes cast on it

statewide.title: Bans new state taxes on owning financial assets and other personal property, and some retroactive taxes
statewide.what: PROHIBITS NEW STATE PERSONAL PROPERTY TAXES AND CERTAIN RETROACTIVE STATE TAXES. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
statewide.yes: The state could not create new taxes on owning stocks, savings or other personal property, and retroactive taxes are limited.
statewide.no: The state keeps the option to create such taxes in the future.
statewide.needs: a simple majority of the votes cast on it

statewide.code: Two-thirds vote for local special taxes
statewide.title: Citizen-proposed local special taxes would need two-thirds of the vote
statewide.what: LIMITS VOTERS’ ABILITY TO RAISE REVENUES FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT SERVICES. LEGISLATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
statewide.yes: Starting in 2027, local special taxes proposed by voters would need two-thirds of the vote to pass.
statewide.no: Local special taxes proposed by voters can still pass with a simple majority.
statewide.needs: a simple majority of the votes cast on it

statewide.title: Nonprofit community clinics must spend 90% of revenue on patient services
statewide.what: REQUIRES COMMUNITY HEALTH CLINICS SPEND 90% OF REVENUE ON PROGRAM SERVICES. INITIATIVE STATUTE.
statewide.yes: Nonprofit community clinics must spend at least 90% of their revenue on health care services or pay the shortfall to the state.
statewide.no: No minimum spending rule for nonprofit community clinics.
statewide.needs: a simple majority of the votes cast on it

statewide.title: Deadlines and narrower lawsuits for environmental review of "essential" projects
statewide.what: MODIFIES ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW FOR CERTAIN PROJECTS. INITIATIVE STATUTE.
statewide.yes: Essential projects can use a faster environmental review with deadlines and narrower lawsuits.
statewide.no: All projects keep using today's environmental review and lawsuit rules.
statewide.needs: a simple majority of the votes cast on it
